candidates.title: RoboEvo^2: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
candidates.content: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo^2, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skills, routing strategies, and experience memory. In Harness-to-Policy (H2P) evolution, verified trajectories provide supervised training, while Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches the policy to favor successful corrections over failures from the same starting state. The improved policy provides stronger motor skills for subsequent search, while its remaining failures redirect harness evolution, closing the reciprocal loop. Through re

candidates.title: 3D CoCa v3: Contrastive Learners with Scene Graphs for Urban Scene Understanding
candidates.content: Understanding large-scale 3D urban scenes requires representations that capture both multi-scale geometric structures and complex spatial relationships. However, existing 3D vision-language methods primarily emphasize global semantic alignment or object-level representations, leaving structured relational modeling underexplored within unified contrastive and generative frameworks. In this paper, we present 3D CoCa v3, a scene-graph-enhanced contrastive and generative framework for urban 3D scene understanding. Our framework features a Pyramid Vision Encoder for multi-scale geometric representation learning and a language-model-based decoder with question-guided caption retrieval and visual cross-attention. We further introduce MSG-based relational descriptions to enrich contrastive 3D-language alignment with structured spatial relationships. To support semantic and relational supervision, we construct City3D-9.6K, a multi-view urban vision-language dataset with aligned visual-geometric observations, scene captions, and scene graphs. Extensive experiments on City-3DQA demonstrate that 3D CoCa v3 achieves 88.35% and 64.79% overall top-1 accuracy on the sentence-wise and city-wise spl

candidates.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
candidates.content: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. candidates.content: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries: With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. Here's the digitized sketchbook . candidates.title: datasette-charts 0.1a0
candidates.content: Release: datasette-charts 0.1a0 I've been thinking about this problem for over a year now, but on Sunday I finally fired up Claude Fable 5.2 to build an initial prototype. The prototype went so well that this is now a full plugin. You can try it out in Datasette Lite here . It looks like this: The new charts plugin works against any table or arbitrary SQL query in Datasette. It defines several different chart types (using vendored D3 , Observable Plot , and topojson-client ), each with a set of heuristics for identifying when they might be a good match for a specific set of rows. Those suggestion thumbnails at the top are actual visualizations driven by the data, and selecting one pulls up the full chart along with tools for modifying it. You can also manually construct a chart from scratch. As with other Datasette visualization plugins, the current state of your chart is persisted in a #fragment in the URL - so you can bookmark charts or share them with others. The most important feature is that the charts take all rows into account . candidates.title: Introducing the Sakana AI Applied Research Lab
candidates.content: （＊日本語は英文の後に） Today we are announcing the Sakana AI Applied Research Lab, a research group within Sakana AI that applies the company’s research to large, complex real-world systems, advancing the state of the art in their understanding and delivering it as value to Sakana AI clients. The Lab’s first program is in finance and economics. We expect other programs to emerge in the future. A complex system, such as a market or an economy, is not something one LLM-powered agentic AI can resolve. A complex phenomenon must be modeled as a system: its units, their links, and how changes in one part affect the others. Deciding which questions to ask, what to model, and how to judge the answers has been the work of human experts, and progress has run at the speed of human effort. Agentic AI can now implement, test, and refine models at scale; its weakness is knowing which questions matter. Combining the two, the potential of AI on top of a foundation of human knowledge, will be the focus of the Lab. candidates.content: [PHASE3] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Pfizer | 适应症: Pneumococcal Disease. The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety of a new pneumococcal vaccine and how the new pneumococcal vaccine helps to fight against germs that can cause pneumonia (lung infections), meningitis (brain infections), and otitis media (ear infections) in infants when compared to the pneumococcal vaccine that is currently in use, 20vPnC (Prevnar 20®). This study will test if the new pneumococcal vaccine is as safe as the one that is currently in use. This new vaccine can possibly provide additional protection against germs that cause pneumococcal disease that are not included in the vaccines that are currently given to infants. Pneumococcal disease includes a variety of infections caused by a specific germ, Streptococcus pneumoniae. There are two groups in this study. All participants will be assigned to one of the two groups. This study is seeking participants who are: \- infants who are about 2 months of age About 2400 infants will be assigned by chance to one of the two groups to receive either PG4 (new vaccine) or 20vPnC (currently in use) into the left thigh muscle at 2, 4, 6, and 12 to 15 months of age.

candidates.title: Endogenous variability in transcription factor concentrations shapes their genome-wide occupancy
candidates.content: Abstract The control of transcription factor (TF) concentrations is crucial for the precise regulation of gene expression and cell fate decisions during development. Yet, TF concentrations can display substantial temporal fluctuations and intercellular variations. How TF levels quantitatively shape genome-wide occupancy patterns remains largely unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate how physiological fluctuations in the concentrations of the pluripotency TFs OCT4, SOX2, and NANOG impact their genomic binding profiles in mouse embryonic stem cells. We uncover distinct concentration-dependent binding behaviors for each TF. NANOG occupancy increased monotonously with its concentration, even though a common set of regions made accessible by OCT4 and SOX2 are highly and uniformly bound at all NANOG concentrations. In contrast, SOX2 occupancy does not increase with its concentrations, while OCT4 displayed an intermediate behavior. Our results challenge the notion that TF binding follows simple mass-action dynamics and reveal a core set of pluripotency regions that are bound by all three TFs at all TF concentrations, revealing how pluripotency can be maintained despite marked flu

candidates.title: AAV-mediated XIST deletion in female human hepatocytes with skewed X-inactivation induces limited reactivation of the X-linked OTC gene in vivo
candidates.content: Abstract Reactivation of silenced wild-type alleles on the inactive X chromosome (Xi) offers a promising therapeutic avenue for X-linked disorders affecting females. The long non-coding RNA XIST is central to Xi silencing, yet its complete loss risks chromosome-wide dosage imbalance. To explore reactivation in a translational context, we employed chimeric mouse–human FRG livers repopulated with primary hepatocytes from a female patient with ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency exhibiting highly skewed X-inactivation. Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated CRISPR–Cas9 delivery was used to disrupt XIST in vivo to assess effects on chromatin landscape and OTC expression. Despite differential XIST promoter methylation, the Xi remained accessible to CRISPR–Cas9, with editing frequencies comparable to those of the active X chromosome. XIST deletion induced limited reactivation of the wild-type OTC allele and was accompanied by broader epigenetic effects. CUT&RUN profiling distinguished effects of vector delivery and XIST deletion, including global H3K4me3 reduction after AAV transduction, X chromosome-restricted H3K27me3 reduction after XIST deletion, and broader H3K27ac reduction

candidates.title: Disease-responsive promoters enable precisely controlled gene therapy
candidates.content: Abstract Adeno associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene therapy holds great promise for curing various diseases, but uncontrolled expression of transgenes in both healthy and diseased cells driven by constitutively active general promoters is a potential safety risk. Controlled gene therapy can be achieved using a disease-responsive promoter (DRP) that drives expression of a therapeutic gene only in diseased cells and shuts off once the cells become healthy again. We used correlative analysis of ATAC-seq and ncRNA-seq of healthy and diseased retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) to identify and characterize two DRPs that possess unique DRP activities in two mouse models of optic neuropathy. We further optimized one DRP to generate DRP-3L2, which has minimum promoter activity in naïve healthy RGCs, but drives potent neuroprotective gene expression in diseased RGCs and then abates after RGCs are protected and returning to health. Our proof-of-concept studies demonstrate that DRP-mediated precisely controlled gene therapy provides a new and promising neuroprotective strategy for CNS axonopathies.

candidates.title: Social predictability increases with age in dolphins: A marker of longevity?
candidates.content: by Erin R. Siracusa Social ageing research has focused on changes in average social behaviour, overlooking behavioural consistency as a trait. A new PLOS Biology study shows that wild dolphins’ grouping patterns become more predictable with age, most markedly in the longest-lived animals. Social aging research has focused on age-related changes in behavioral averages, overlooking behavioral consistency as a trait. This Primer explores a new PLOS Biology showing that grouping patterns become more predictable with age in dolphins, and links this pattern to longevity.

candidates.content: arXiv:2611.33497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. We propose Constraint-Aligned RAG (CA-RAG), a retrieval-conditioning framework that augments section-specific queries with ontology-derived structural constraints and policy-grounded knowledge-graph relations before evidence selection. Retrieval-only evaluation with manually annotated evidence shows consistent improvements across retrieval budgets. At $k=6$, CA-RAG increases Precision@$k$ from $0.5268$ to $0.5692$, pooled Recall@$k$ from $0.5402$ to $0.5950$, and F1@$k$ from $0.5389$ to $0.5672$ over standard RAG. candidates.content: arXiv:2611.34432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aviation accident narratives contain safety knowledge that is difficult to capture using structured occurrence fields alone. This study evaluates prompting-based knowledge extraction across four dimensions: concept accuracy, verbatim evidence grounding, structural compliance, and directed relation extraction. SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct was evaluated under zero-shot, one-shot, fixed few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting using 300 National Transportation Safety Board narratives from 2000-2020, containing 3,763 reference concepts and 467 directed relations. Evaluation combined structural checks, verbatim evidence matching, expert-reviewed semantic matching, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals. No prompting strategy performed best across all dimensions. candidates.title: Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge to Guide Continual Learning
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.33399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to adapt to new data (plasticity) while retaining the knowledge acquired from old data (stability). Existing methods are explicitly designed to focus on balancing stability and plasticity to mitigate the challenge of catastrophic forgetting while promoting learning. However, the impact of order and nature of samples from the new data that the network is trained on remains an under explored factor. We argue that a CL algorithm should have the ability to rank incoming samples in terms of their relationship with prior data and their effect on the learning process. In this work, we investigate if scoring and prioritizing incoming data based on their semantic relationships with the model's current knowledge can benefit CL. We propose SACK, short for Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge, a plug and play technique for continual learning methods. SACK dissects categorical knowledge of the model into fine-grained concepts, computes the relationships between previously learned concepts and new concepts in each experience, and uses this relationship knowledge for prioritizing new samples. candidates.content: arXiv:2611.34416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots executing tasks in partially observed environments must resolve uncertainty while operating with incomplete skills. Inspired by human curiosity, we investigate how robots can formulate task-relevant hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution. We propose CHASE, a Curiosity-guided Harness for Acquiring Skills from Evidence, which operationalizes curiosity as selecting investigations that resolve task uncertainty and expand executable capabilities. Four modules connect dynamic scene understanding, hypothesis-driven planning, on-demand skill acquisition, and verified execution. The planner balances information value, skill reuse, and acquisition/execution cost. Missing skills trigger bounded exploration, learning from verified segments, and held-out admission during acquisition; separate checks verify physical effects and acquired evidence. Newly admitted skills expand the executable investigation set, closing the loop between resolving uncertainty and acquiring capabilities. candidates.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
candidates.content: arXiv:2607.23586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Long-lived AI agents increasingly evolve after deployment by retaining experience, acquiring skills and tools, revising workflows, delegating work, and moving across task phases. This improves adaptation but creates a distinct authorization problem. Tool-enabled agents can turn model errors and prompt injections into consequential external actions; when evolution occurs under a live grant, the subject exercising that authority or the context in which it acts may no longer match what the user evaluated. Evolution can change both the effects reachable under an old grant and the authority required by the task, which may rise, fall, or become incomparable. Existing tool policies constrain actions but do not determine when a grant survives this change. We formulate authorization continuity: when does an existing grant remain valid, how may active authority change, and what boundary must never move? candidates.title: AESP: A Human-Sovereign Economic Protocol for AI Agents with Privacy-Preserving Settlement
candidates.content: arXiv:2603.00318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As AI agents increasingly perform economic tasks on behalf of humans, a fundamental tension arises between agent autonomy and human control over financial assets. We present the Agent Economic Sovereignty Protocol (AESP), a layered protocol in which agents transact autonomously at machine speed on crypto-native infrastructure while remaining cryptographically bound to human-defined governance boundaries. AESP enforces the invariant that agents are economically capable but never economically sovereign through five mechanisms: (1) a deterministic eight-check policy engine with tiered escalation; (2) human-in-the-loop review with automatic, explicit, and biometric tiers; (3) EIP-712 dual-signed commitments with escrow; (4) HKDF-based context-isolated privacy with batched consolidation; and (5) an ACE-GF-based cryptographic substrate. We formalize two testable hypotheses on security coverage and latency overhead, and specify a complete evaluation methodology with baselines and ablation design. The protocol is implemented as an open-source TypeScript SDK (208 tests, ten modules) with interoperability via MCP and A2A.
